name: Fundamentals
description: Core programming concepts and basic algorithmic patterns. The building blocks every programmer must master.
tooltip: Essential algorithms every programmer should know

name: Sorting
description: Algorithms that arrange data elements in a specific order. Essential for optimizing search operations and data organization.
tooltip: Arrange data in ascending or descending order

name: Searching
description: Algorithms for locating specific elements within data structures. Different approaches optimize for different data arrangements.
tooltip: Find elements efficiently in data structures

name: Array & String
description: Algorithms for manipulating arrays and strings — the most fundamental data structures in programming.

name: Linked Lists
description: Algorithms operating on linked list data structures. Master pointer manipulation and dynamic memory concepts.
tooltip: Work with node-based linear data structures

name: Stack & Queue
description: LIFO and FIFO data structure algorithms. Essential for parsing, scheduling, and graph traversal.
tooltip: LIFO and FIFO operations and applications

name: Hashing
description: Hash-based algorithms enabling O(1) average-time operations. The foundation of fast lookups and caching.

name: Trees
description: Tree data structure algorithms — from basic traversals to balanced BSTs, tries, and segment trees.

name: Heaps
description: Heap-based algorithms for priority-based operations. Essential for scheduling, graph algorithms, and order statistics.

name: Graphs
description: Graph traversal and shortest-path algorithms. Model networks, relationships, and pathways in real-world systems.

name: Greedy
description: Algorithms that make locally optimal choices at each step. Simple, fast, and surprisingly effective for many problems.
tooltip: Make optimal local choices for global solutions

name: Dynamic Programming
description: Optimization technique breaking problems into overlapping subproblems. Master memoization and tabulation for efficient solutions.
tooltip: Optimize via overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure

name: Backtracking
description: Systematic trial-and-error algorithms that explore all possibilities. Essential for constraint satisfaction and combinatorial problems.

name: Advanced
description: Advanced algorithms including string matching, computational geometry, and complex data structures.
